ideas.diversification_value: Unlike existing regime filters which use a single metric (Hurst, ATR, yield curve, gamma), this is a multi-indicator consensus system. It can also switch between momentum and mean-reversion internally, making it a meta-strategy overlay rather than a single-entry logic. No existing bot in the archive combines multiple classification inputs into a regime-aware multi-mode system.

ideas.name: False_Breakout_Trap_Fade
ideas.description: Anti-breakout strategy that detects false breakouts — price breaks a key structural level (swing high/low, order block, or previous session high/low) but immediately reverses with a long upper/lower wick, forming a trap. Entries are in the opposite direction of the failed breakout, capitalizing on trapped liquidity.
ideas.entry_logic: 1) Identify key structural levels: previous H1 swing high/low (last 48 bars), previous Asian session high/low, or visible order block. 2) Price breaks the level by at least 0.3x ATR(14). 3) Within 3 bars of the break, price closes back inside the level, leaving a wick of at least 0.5x ATR beyond the level. 4) The break bar and the reversal bar must both have above-average volume (>20 SMA of volume). 5) Enter on close of the reversal bar in the direction opposite to the breakout (long if false breakout below support, short if false breakout above resistance). 6) Invalidated if price closes beyond the wick extreme.
ideas.exit_logic: Stop loss: 0.5x ATR beyond the wick extreme (tight — the trap level is the hard invalidation). Take profit: 1) 50% at 1x ATR from entry; 2) 50% at 1.5x ATR trailing stop (activate after 0.8x ATR move). Maximum risk per trade: 0.5% of account. Hard stop at end of trading session.
ideas.failure_mode: Strong trending markets produce few clean false breakouts — the strategy goes dormant for days. The tight stop means many small losses can accumulate in choppy conditions where false breakouts are common but directionless. Requires precise structural level identification — ambiguous levels increase false signal rate. Whipsaw in high-volatility events (news) where initial break and reversal are both liquidity grabs in the same direction as the broader trend.
ideas.diversification_value: Every existing breakout bot in the archive trades WITH the breakout direction. This is the only strategy that trades AGAINST false breakouts — it profits from trapped breakout traders. Its success is inversely correlated with strong trend-following breakout bots: when false breakouts are frequent, trend-following breakouts are losing money, and vice versa. This provides true non-correlation within the breakout family.

ideas.name: Session_Initial_Balance_Breakout
ideas.description: Session-anchored breakout strategy using the Initial Balance (IB) — the high-low range of the first 60 minutes of each major trading session (Asian 00:00-01:00 UTC, London 07:00-08:00 UTC, New York 13:00-14:00 UTC). Breakouts beyond the IB range with confirmed momentum are traded in the breakout direction, with targets defined by statistical session volatility profiles.
ideas.entry_logic: 1) At the start of Asian (00:00 UTC), London (07:00 UTC), and New York (13:00 UTC) sessions, record the Initial Balance: highest high and lowest low of the first 4 x M15 candles (60 min). 2) Wait for price to break beyond the IB high or low by 0.2x ATR(14). 3) Confirm with M15 RSI(7) > 65 (long) or < 35 (short) — must be above/below threshold at the time of breakout. 4) The breakout candle must close beyond the IB level (not just wick through). 5) Enter on the next M15 open with limit order at the IB level (entry on retest/break). 6) No re-entries — each session gets one attempt in each direction.
ideas.exit_logic: Stop loss: 0.8x ATR(14) from entry (below IB for long, above IB for short). Take profit: Session-dependent — Asian session: 1.2x ATR (Asian ranges are smaller); London session: 2.0x ATR (widest range); New York session: 1.5x ATR. Trailing stop activates after 1x ATR profit moves, trail by 0.3x ATR. Hard exit at session end (Asian: 08:00 UTC, London: 16:00 UTC, New York: 21:00 UTC) — no overnight holds.
ideas.failure_mode: Low-volatility days where price never breaks the IB range produce zero trades. Session overlap periods (London-New York 13:00-16:00 UTC) can produce conflicting signals if both sessions have active IB levels. Holidays and shortened sessions distort the initial balance calculation. The fixed session-end exit means profitable trades in strong trend can get cut short before full move.
ideas.diversification_value: Unlike existing breakout strategies (London_Killzone_Breakout, Asian_Session_Breakout_Continuation, Volume_Profile_Acceptance_Breakout), this combines session-specific IB calculation with session-dependent TP targets based on statistical volatility profiles per session. No existing bot in the archive adapts its profit target to the specific session's historical range characteristics.

ideas.name: Momentum_Carry_Volatility_Filter
ideas.description: Combines trend-momentum entry with a positive carry filter (contango/backwardation in gold futures basis) and uses ATR-normalized volatility gating to prevent entry during choppy or overextended conditions. The idea: strong trends that also have favourable carry (futures curve in backwardation) and moderate volatility (not too low = no trend, not too high = blow-off top) are the highest-probability momentum trades.
ideas.entry_logic: Step 1: Calculate 50-period and 200-period EMA slope on XAUUSD H1/H4. A bullish slope requires EMA50 > EMA200 and both sloping up. Step 2: Compute gold futures basis (front-month futures price / spot price). Require basis > 1.001 (backwardation, positive carry) for longs or basis < 0.999 (contango, negative carry) for shorts. Step 3: Compute 14-period ATR as % of price. Gate: only trade if ATR% is between its 20-period 30th and 70th percentile — kills zero-volatility flat markets and blow-off top volatility spikes. Step 4: On aligned H1 trend, wait for a pullback to 20 EMA with a bullish engulfing or hammer candle. Entry on close of confirmation candle.
ideas.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1.5x ATR(14) below entry. Take profit: 3:1 risk-reward, or trail stop at 1x ATR once price moves 2x ATR in profit. Time stop: close after 48 bars if neither hit. Additional exit: if basis flips (carry changes sign) with price still in trade, reduce to half position.
ideas.failure_mode: Can whipsaw during contango/backwardation regime shifts when central bank policy changes rapidly (e.g. surprise rate cuts/hikes). The volatility percentile gate may also miss the first powerful leg of a new trend until the next pullback.
ideas.diversification_value: Uniquely adds positive carry as a momentum confirmatory filter — no existing momentum bot in the archive uses the gold futures basis curve. Also uses volatility percentile gating rather than raw ATR thresholds, preventing overfitted parameter drift.

ideas.name: Mean_Reversion_OrderFlow_Exhaustion
ideas.description: Identifies short-term exhaustion points in gold by combining tick-volume delta divergence with cluster-wide wick structure. When aggressive buying (delta divergence — price makes higher high but cumulative delta makes lower high) coincides with an identifiable liquidity sweep wick through a recent swing high, the market has exhausted the marginal buyer and is primed for a mean-reversion snap back toward the value area (VWAP or 20 EMA on M15).
ideas.entry_logic: Step 1: On M15, compute cumulative delta divergence — price makes a swing high above the prior 20-bar high while cumulative delta (aggressive buys - aggressive sells over 5 bars) fails to confirm, printing a lower high. Step 2: Confirm the high candle has a wick at least 2x the body length and the wick extended at least 0.5 ATR beyond the prior 20-bar high (liquidity sweep pattern). Step 3: Volume on the exhaustion bar must be in the top 30% of 50-bar volume (shows real participation, not noise). Step 4: Enter short on close of the exhaustion bar. For long entries, reverse: price makes lower low with delta making higher low, wick sweeps below prior 20-bar low, high volume.
ideas.exit_logic: Stop loss: 0.5 ATR beyond the swept liquidity level (above the wick high). Take profit: 1:1.5 risk-reward or VWAP whichever comes first. If price re-enters the wick zone (invalidates the sweep), exit immediately at market. Hard time stop: 24 bars.
ideas.failure_mode: Fails in strong trending one-directional markets where delta divergence can persist for many bars (trend exhaustion not the same as mean-reversion exhaustion). Entries against a strong trend get crushed. Needs a regime filter (e.g. ADX < 30) as a prerequisite.
ideas.diversification_value: Introduces cumulative delta divergence as a formal entry mechanism — no existing mean-reversion idea uses order-flow delta data. Also uniquely requires wick-to-body ratio (liquidity sweep) as a confirmation condition, bridging order-flow analysis with price structure.

ideas.name: Cross_Asset_Basis_Divergence
ideas.description: Exploits divergence between gold-silver ratio momentum and the US Dollar Index movement. The logic: when XAU/XAG ratio is rising (gold outperforming silver — typically risk-off behaviour) but DXY is falling (bearish dollar — typically risk-on behaviour), there is an inter-asset inconsistency that historically resolves with gold catching down or silver catching up. This cross-asset basis divergence acts as an early warning that the current gold move is fragile and likely to mean-revert or stall.
ideas.entry_logic: Step 1: Compute the 21-period rate of change of the XAU/XAG ratio (gold price / silver price) on H4. Step 2: Compute the 21-period rate of change of DXY on H4. Step 3: Divergence signal occurs when ROC_XAUXAG > +5% (gold strongly outperforming silver) AND ROC_DXY < -2% (dollar weakening). This is the inconsistency — risk-off in metals (gold beating silver) while risk-on in FX (bearish USD). Step 4: (a) If gold is above its 50 EMA on D1, favour short gold (risk-off priced into gold, USD weakness should pull commodities up but silver is already being bought — gold is the laggard). (b) If gold is below 50 EMA on D1, go long silver (silver will catch up when risk-on returns). Entry on close of the bar where divergence exceeds both thresholds.
ideas.exit_logic: Stop loss: 1% below entry for gold shorts, 1.5% below entry for silver longs. Take profit: when either ROC_XAUXAG drops below +2% or ROC_DXY rises above 0% — the divergence has resolved. Hard stop at 20 bars. Scale out 50% at 1:1 risk-reward, trail the rest at 1 ATR.
ideas.failure_mode: Central bank interventions (e.g. BOJ/Fed coordinated dollar operations) can distort DXY beyond normal correlation regimes. Also, the XAU/XAG ratio can diverge from the dollar for extended periods during sustained gold bull runs driven by physical demand (central bank buying, not speculative). Works best in normal speculative environments.
ideas.diversification_value: Uniquely exploits the XAU/XAG ratio in tandem with DXY in an inconsistency-detection framework. No existing cross_asset idea uses this specific three-asset divergence (gold vs silver vs dollar) as a signal. Also proposes asset-direction switching (short gold vs long silver) based on trend context — adaptive cross-asset hedging.

ideas.name: Volatility_Momentum_Inflection
ideas.description: Tracks the speed of volatility change (ATR rate-of-change) rather than absolute volatility level. Enters long-vol when deceleration flips to acceleration, short-vol when acceleration peaks and turns. Leading inflection signal that pairs with any directional bot.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Compute ATR(14) and its ROC(5) over 5 bars. 2. Track ATR_ROC(5) as histogram. When ROC > +15% for 3 consecutive bars (over-expanded), flag ready. 3. On first bar where ATR_ROC(5) turns negative while ATR still elevated - go SHORT vol (mean-reversion mode). 4. When ATR_ROC(5) below -10% for 3 bars then turns positive - go LONG vol (momentum-breakout mode). 5. Only trade when ROC crosses ±10% threshold.
ideas.exit_logic: SL at 2x ATR(14) from entry price. TP at 1x ATR(14) or when ATR_ROC(5) returns to ±3% neutral zone. Max hold 20 bars. Trailing stop at 1.5x ATR once in profit by 0.5x ATR.
ideas.failure_mode: In prolonged trending volatility that keeps accelerating (e.g. sustained crisis), inflection fires too early, catching the wrong side repeatedly. False signals in choppy sideways vol where ROC oscillates around zero.
ideas.diversification_value: Only idea tracking speed-of-change of volatility rather than absolute level or direction. Non-directional timing overlay that pairs with any existing directional bot. Unique among 9 existing vol ideas.

ideas.name: Liquidity_Regime_Filter
ideas.description: Market regime defined by liquidity conditions rather than trend/volatility. Uses tick volume normalized by ATR and bid-ask spread proxy to classify High/Normal/Low liquidity. Only trades during high liquidity when execution quality supports edges; flattens in low liquidity stop-hunting zones.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Compute Liquidity Score every 15 min: (tick_volume / ATR(14)) to normalize volume over range. 2. Compute Spread Proxy: 1-min bar range % of ATR(14) - wider bars relative to ATR = illiquidity. 3. Liquidity Index = (Volume_ratio_EMA10 × 0.6) + (Spread_zscore_EMA10 × 0.4). 4. High liquidity > +0.5, Low < -0.5, Neutral zone in between. 5. Enter trades only in High liquidity. Mandatory flat on Low liquidity.
ideas.exit_logic: Standard trade exits per base strategy. Mandatory flat signal when LI drops below -0.5. Re-entry only when LI recovers above +0.5 (not just crosses -0.5). Time-stops: max 4hrs in Low liquidity regime.
ideas.failure_mode: During flash crashes or black-swan events, liquidity disappears in seconds - the filter reacts after the fact, locking in losses before LI drops. Tick volume proxy unreliable on MT4 free tick data.
ideas.diversification_value: Novel regime dimension - liquidity. No existing regime_filter idea uses liquidity as primary axis. Orthogonal to trend/vol/Hurst/cluster regimes. Filters all directional families at the top level.

ideas.name: Conviction_Variance_Contractor
ideas.description: Dynamic position-sizing overlay that contracts capital on signals with historically high outcome variance and expands on signals with tight, reliable outcomes. Measures R-multiple standard deviation across the last 30 trades per signal ID and scales position as (Mean_R / σ_R) ratio - essentially per-signal Sharpe scaling.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Per active strategy/signal ID, maintain rolling lookup of last 30 trades with R-multiple outcomes. 2. Compute R-multiple std dev (σ_R) of the table. 3. Conviction Score = Mean_R / σ_R (per-trade Sharpe). 4. Baseline position scaled: Conviction_Size = Base_Size × (Score / Target_Conviction), clamped [0.25×, 2.0×]. 5. Time-decay: trades >60 days contribute 50% less weight to the table.
ideas.exit_logic: Overlay only - not a trade exit. Risk management via capital allocation. Max 2.0× leverage on high conviction, min 0.25× (nearly flat) on poor conviction. Snowball stops: if 3 consecutive trades from same signal lose >1R each, halve that signal allocation for 30 trades.
ideas.failure_mode: Small sample problem - <10 trades yields unreliable Conviction Score oscillating wildly. Regime shift invalidates past reliability assumptions. Over-optimizes to recent performance in trending then whipsawing markets.
ideas.diversification_value: Bridges signal quality to capital allocation uniquely. Unlike Kelly (stationary distribution assumed) or VaR/vol-parity (ignores signal quality entirely). Pure signal-adaptive risk overlay.

ideas.name: Index_Structural_Breakout
ideas.description: US index structural breakout using the 09:30-10:30 EST opening range. When price breaks beyond the opening range with 1.5x ATR candle confirmation and RSI(14) directional filter (55/45 threshold), it captures sustained intraday directional flow during US cash hours (14:30-21:00 UTC). First non-XAUUSD breakout in the archive.
ideas.entry_logic: 1) Compute opening range H/L from 09:30-10:30 EST on H1 chart. 2) Wait for candle to close beyond opening range with candle range >=1.5x ATR(20). 3) Confirm RSI(14) >55 (long) or <45 (short) — filters overbought/oversold false breaks. 4) Enter on close of breakout candle. 5) Skip if opening range width <15 pts (low vol) or >60 pts (event distortion).
ideas.exit_logic: SL at opposite side of opening range. TP1 at 1.5x opening range width, TP2 at 2.5x. 20-period ATR trailing stop activated after TP1 hit. Hard stop-loss — no breakeven until TP1.
ideas.failure_mode: High-impact macro data (FOMC, NFP, CPI) during US session invalidates opening range structure. Gaps at 09:30 EST create false breakouts. Works poorly in tight sideways ranging days.
ideas.diversification_value: First non-XAUUSD breakout idea in the archive. Trades US indices with US-session structural method — uncorrelated to Asian/London gold breakouts. Zero overlap with existing XAUUSD breakout strategies.

ideas.name: Cross_Commodity_Seasonal_Rotation
ideas.description: Cross-commodity seasonal rotation trading silver, platinum, and palladium on their strongest calendar month patterns. Silver bullish Mar/May/Nov/Dec, platinum bullish Sep/Oct/Nov, palladium bullish Feb/Mar. Enters the metal with the strongest current-month tailwind confirmed above 50-day SMA. First multi-commodity seasonal strategy in the archive.
ideas.entry_logic: 1) On first trading day of each month, check historical seasonal bias: Silver bullish Mar/May/Nov/Dec, Platinum bullish Sep/Oct/Nov, Palladium bullish Feb/Mar. 2) Select the metal with strongest current-month tailwind. 3) Confirm price above 50-day SMA for long entries. 4) If no metal has a clear seasonal edge that month, stay flat. 5) Enter at market open on day 1.
ideas.exit_logic: Hard SL at 2x ATR(20). TP at end-of-month close. Partial exit 50% at 1x ATR if reached before month-end, remainder held to EOM. If position >3% profit by mid-month, lock breakeven stop on remaining position.
ideas.failure_mode: Synchronized macro shock (COVID, 2008, systemic crisis) overrides all commodity seasonal patterns simultaneously. USD strength spike can invalidate all three metals. Thin liquidity in XPT/XPD causes slippage.
ideas.diversification_value: First non-XAUUSD seasonal idea. Trades silver, platinum, palladium on rotation — completely uncorrelated to gold seasonal patterns. First multi-commodity seasonal rotation strategy in the archive. Opens the seasonal family to industrial precious metals.

ideas.name: Forex_Carry_Volatility_Compression
ideas.description: Forex volatility compression-expansion strategy tied to carry trade dynamics. When ATR(14) percentile drops below the 20th percentile of its 50-bar range on H4 for 3+ consecutive bars, the subsequent expansion is directional — typically reversing the prior carry direction. Trades the expansion with a bias opposite the compression-phase drift.
ideas.entry_logic: 1) Compute ATR(14) on H4 and its percentile rank over 50-bar lookback. 2) When ATR percentile stays <20 for 3 consecutive bars, flag as compressed. 3) Measure net change over last 10 bars: if up >0.5% during compression, prepare short; if down >0.5%, prepare long. 4) Enter on the bar where ATR(14) expands above its 50-period median — direction opposite the compression drift. 5) Trade only the pair with the highest composite compression score.
ideas.exit_logic: SL at 1.5x the compressed-range ATR(14). TP at 2.0x compressed ATR range. If profit reaches 1x range within 6 bars post-entry, move SL to breakeven. Maximum hold: 24 bars on H4.
ideas.failure_mode: Central bank surprise (rate hike/cut) during compression creates violent move outside anticipated direction, slamming both sides. USDCAD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD are more carry-sensitive — EURUSD/GBPUSD/USDJPY chosen to mitigate this. Fails in strong trending markets with no compression phases.
ideas.diversification_value: First forex-pair volatility idea in the archive — all 10 existing volatility ideas are XAUUSD-only. First carry-related volatility compression model. Low correlation to gold vol strategies. Opens the volatility family to major forex pairs.

ideas.name: Momentum_Exhaustion_Entropy_Decay
ideas.description: Fades momentum at exhaustion point by detecting entropy divergence — when Chaikin Money Flow (CMF) diverges bearishly from price while volume distribution entropy spikes, it signals momentum is running out of fuel and a snap-back is imminent. Unlike pure trend-following momentum strategies, this catches the inflection BEFORE the reversal gains steam.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Calculate 20-period CMF and 14-period RSI on H1. 2. Track whether price made a higher high (uptrend) or lower low (downtrend) in the last 3 bars. 3. DIVERGENCE CHECK: price made higher high but CMF made lower high (bearish divergence) AND RSI < 70 (not overbought) → prepares for SHORT. Inverse for longs. 4. ENTROPY CHECK: Calculate volume distribution entropy over last 20 periods using Shannon entropy on normalized volume buckets (H = -sum(p_i * log2(p_i))). Entropy > 3.2 (top quartile of 200-period history) confirms disorder — smart money distribution is fragmenting. 5. ENTRY: On M15, wait for a failed breakout candle (long wick > 60% of candle range in direction opposite to the prior trend) in the divergence zone. Enter 1 pip inside the wick tip. 6. Tiered sizing: base 0.5% risk, double to 1% if entropy is in top decile (strongest exhaustion signal).
ideas.exit_logic: SL: Below the divergence swing low (longs) or above swing high (shorts) PLUS 0.5× H1 ATR buffer. TP1: 1.5× H1 ATR (50% position). TP2: Next structural swing level identified from 48-hour range (30% position). TP3: Trail remaining 20% with 1× H1 ATR chandelier stop. Time-stop: if TP1 not hit within 6 hours, close remaining at market. If profit exceeds 2× ATR before TP1, move SL to breakeven on all positions.
ideas.failure_mode: Fails hardest during trending news events (NFP, FOMC, CPI) where momentum is fundamental and sustained — CMF divergence persists for days before any reversal, entropy stays high without mean-reverting. Also fails in extreme trend-strength regimes (ADX > 45) where exhaustion signals are premature and get steamrolled. The entropy threshold needs recalibration during holiday low-volume periods when entropy is naturally elevated.
ideas.diversification_value: Radically different from all 10 existing momentum ideas — those are pure trend-following/continuation strategies (MSS_Continuation, Donchian_Breakout, ADX_Trend_Momentum, Vanna_Flow). This is the FIRST anti-momentum momentum idea: it exploits momentum EXHAUSTION rather than momentum PERSISTENCE. It is the momentum equivalent of fade/countertrend — orthogonal to the entire momentum category. It pairs naturally with Momentum_Confluence_Gold (which enters early trend) as a complementary exit signal.

ideas.name: Liquidity_Tier_Volatility_Contraction_Pinball
ideas.description: Exploits the pattern where price pinballs between pre-identified liquidity tiers (key levels from volume profile high-node areas) while volatility contracts sequentially on each touch. As volatility contracts, the eventual break becomes explosive. This is fundamentally different from standard volatility contraction setups (Bollinger squeeze) because it incorporates structural liquidity zone geometry.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. BUILD LIQUIDITY TIERS: On H1, identify volume profile high-volume nodes (HVN) — price levels where >1.5× average volume traded over last 5 days. Mark the 3 nearest HVNs above and below current price. These are the "liquidity pinball walls." 2. MEASURE SESSION VOLATILITY: Calculate 20-period ATR on M15. Compute the ratio: current 15-bar ATR / 100-bar ATR (volatility contraction ratio, VCR). 3. PINBALL STATE: Price must have touched at least TWO liquidity tiers in alternating direction within the last 8 hours (e.g., hit HVN_Upper, then HVN_Lower, then back toward HVN_Upper). 4. CONTRACTION FILTER: VCR must be < 0.70 (volatility is contracting compared to medium-term). 5. ENTRY: On the THIRD touch of any liquidity tier, if VCR < 0.65 (further contracted), enter 1 pip beyond that tier in the direction of the bounce. If VCR is 0.65-0.70, wait for a confirming M5 candle close outside the tier. 6. SCALING: If VCR < 0.55 (extreme contraction), double position size — break is expected to be violent.
ideas.exit_logic: SL: Opposite side of the originating liquidity tier (if entered at HVN_Upper bounce, SL is 1 pip below HVN_Lower). This gives the pinball pattern room to reverse. TP1: 1× the distance between the two most recent liquidity tiers (the "pinball range"), measured from entry. TP2: 2× pinball range. Move SL to breakeven when TP1 is hit and price is still moving in direction. If price fails to reach TP1 within 3 hours, exit at market — the pinball pattern has decayed into a range.
ideas.failure_mode: Fails in directional trending markets where price blows through liquidity tiers without bouncing (no pinball behavior). Fails in ultra-low-volatility environments (Asian session) where VCR < 0.50 is common but the subsequent break has no follow-through. Most critically, fails when new liquidity tiers are being formed (breaking price discovery) — the HVN levels become obsolete. Heavy data dependency: the volume profile calculation window (5 days) can lag into regime changes.
ideas.diversification_value: Entirely different from all 11 existing volatility ideas. Those cover: volatility expansion breakout, volatility skew mean reversion, term structure fade, momentum ride, implied/realized spread, event straddle, risk premium decay, put/call skew, VWAP vol channel, vol momentum inflection, and carry compression. NONE of them incorporate structural liquidity zone geometry or pinball-tier mechanics. This is the first volatility strategy that combines level geometry with contraction dynamics — it sits at the intersection of volatility, market microstructure, and volume profile analysis.

ideas.name: Macro_Minsky_Moment_Regime_Shift
ideas.description: Detects impending regime shifts using the Minsky Moment framework — when leverage/debt metrics across intermarket proxies reach extreme levels, a sudden deleveraging event (Minsky Moment) is imminent, flipping gold from risk-on to risk-off dynamics (or vice versa). Unlike conventional regime filters that react to vol/Hurst/yield-curve changes, this PREDICTS the regime shift before price reflects it.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. BUILD MINKSY STRESS INDEX (MSI): Combine three normalized proxies tracked daily: (a) HY-IG credit spread percentile over 2 years, (b) 3-month LIBOR-OIS spread or equivalent (SOFR-OIS) percentile over 2 years, (c) Gold leasing rate (GOFO backwardation) intensity over 2 years. MSI = average of the three percentiles (0-100). 2. REGIME STATE: Baseline = Normal (MSI < 60). Elevated Stress (MSI 60-80). Minsky Zone (MSI > 80). 3. SHIFT DETECTION: A Minsky Moment is signaled when MSI crosses from Elevated Stress into Minsky Zone (>80) AND gold has rallied >5% in the prior 30 days (risk-on positioning is vulnerable). This predicts a FLIGHT-TO-CASH deleveraging → gold sells off even though it is a traditional safe haven. INVERSE: When MSI drops from Minsky Zone below 60 AND gold has sold off >5% in the prior 30 days, predicts regime shift back to normal → gold rebounds as liquidity returns. 4. ENTRY: On H4, enter at market open of the first 4-hour candle after the MSI cross is confirmed at daily close (30 min after New York close). 5. CONFIRMATION: Require that H4 RSI(14) is not extreme (>75 for short, <25 for long) — if extreme, wait for a pullback to the 20 EMA before entering.
ideas.exit_logic: SL: 3× H4 ATR(20). TP: Hold until MSI drops below 60 (for deleveraging shorts) or MSI rises above 80 (for liquidity-recovery longs), OR 14 days have passed — whichever comes first. If profit exceeds 5× ATR within 48 hours, take 50% profit and move SL to entry on remainder. This is a macro swing trade, not a scalp — wide stops are intentional.
ideas.failure_mode: Most critical failure: central bank intervention (Fed QE, swap lines, gold price caps) can suppress the deleveraging signal — MSI spikes but gold does not sell off because liquidity is injected artificially. The 2008 GFC and 2020 COVID examples worked, but 2023 SVB failure did NOT produce gold deleveraging (gold rallied instead due to rate-cut expectations). Also fails in extended periods of financial repression where credit spreads stay artificially low. The 2-year lookback window on percentiles creates lag — if a new stress regime is structurally different from past 2 years, percentiles mislead.
ideas.diversification_value: Fundamentally different from all 10 existing regime filters. Those are: ATR percentile regimes, macro-regime shifter (GDP/CPI based), Hurst exponent, volatility clusters, fractal phase transitions, yield curve regime switch, intermarket vol breakdown, gamma flip, cluster consensus, and liquidity regime filter. NONE of them use a Minsky/crisis-prediction framework. This is the ONLY predictive (vs reactive) regime filter — it anticipates the regime shift rather than confirming it after price has already reacted. It operates on a D1 cadence whereas all others are intraday or daily. It also uniquely treats regime transitions as TRADEABLE EVENTS (direction entry) rather than as filters applied to other strategies.

ideas.name: Momentum_ROC_Acceleration_Confluence
ideas.description: Captures trending breakouts by detecting acceleration in Rate-of-Change (ROC) slopes across 3 lookback periods (5, 13, 34), confirmed by volume impulse and ATR-scaled price position above VWAP. Aims to catch momentum just as it inflects higher, before the move is obvious to lagging indicators.
ideas.entry_logic: 1) Calculate ROC(5), ROC(13), ROC(34) — all three must be rising (monotonic acceleration). 2) Price must be > VWAP by at least 0.5 ATR (long) or < VWAP by 0.5 ATR (short). 3) Volume tick-count spike > 1.5x MA(20) volume. 4) M15 pullback must not violate the 34-period SMA. Enter on H1 close.
ideas.exit_logic: Trailing stop at 1.5 ATR from H1 high/low. Take partial at 2:1 RR (50% position). Remaining trails via parabolic SAR. Hard stop-loss at 2 ATR. No counter-trend add.
ideas.failure_mode: Choppy trendless markets where ROC fluctuates at random — false acceleration signals followed by immediate reversal. Best with a regime filter (ADX > 25) to gate entries.
ideas.diversification_value: Uses ROC slope acceleration rather than ADX or Donchian. Captures the inflection point rather than the established trend, reducing lag vs. Momentum_Confluence_Gold and MultiTimeframe_ADX_Trend_Momentum.

ideas.name: ZScore_ATR_Mean_Reverter
ideas.description: Exploits statistical over-extension in gold by entering when price deviates >2.0 standard deviations from its 50-period SMA (Z-score), with confirmation that the deviation is ATR-proportional and order flow is decelerating. Targets reversion to the mean without catching a falling knife.
ideas.entry_logic: 1) Z-score of close vs SMA(50) exceeds +2.0 (short) or -2.0 (long). 2) ATR(14) must be in the 40-70th percentile of its 50-day range (not panic-mode). 3) Volume tick-count on the deviation bar must be declining vs prior 3 bars (exhaustion signature). 4) M15 RSI(14) must be > 70 (short) or < 30 (long). Enter on first bar where Z-score drops below 1.8 on the opposite side.
ideas.exit_logic: Target: SMA(50) (Z-score = 0). Hard stop at Z-score > 3.0 (short) or < -3.0 (long). If price closes beyond 3.0 Z-score, exit immediately as statistical breakdown. Time stop: exit if not hit target within 24 bars.
ideas.failure_mode: Strong trending breakouts that blow through the 3-sigma band (e.g. NFP surprises, war events). The 3.0 hard stop limits losses but catches the full spike. Also, Z-score oscillates around 1.5-2.0 range frequently in high-vol regimes without reverting.
ideas.diversification_value: Statistically-grounded Z-score approach differs from the RSI divergence, VWAP, or order-flow-only reversion ideas. Explicitly guards against catching strong trends with the 3-sigma breakdown exit. No other idea uses Z-score as the primary trigger.

ideas.name: ADX_Volatility_Regime_Composite
ideas.description: Classifies the market into 4 regimes using a 2D matrix of ADX(14) strength (< 25 = ranging, >= 25 = trending) and volatility percentile (ATR percentile of 50-day range: < 40th = compressing, > 60th = expanding, else neutral). Each quadrant assigns a dedicated sub-strategy to match conditions: ranging/compressing = squeeze breakout, ranging/expanding = mean reversion, trending/compressing = continuation, trending/expanding = momentum ride.
ideas.entry_logic: 1) Calculate ADX(14) and ATR(14) percentile over last 50 bars. 2) Classify quadrant: Ranging+Compressing = Bollinger squeeze breakout on M15; Ranging+Expanding = Z-score mean reversion on H1; Trending+Compressing = pullback-to-20-EMA on H1; Trending+Expanding = momentum continue with trailing stop. 3) Entries only when regime has been stable for 3+ bars (no flip-flop).
ideas.exit_logic: Exit when regime quadrant changes (regime overlay exits the position). Each sub-strategy uses its own SL/TP (1.5-2 ATR range). No pegging to a single take-profit — regime change is the exit signal.
ideas.failure_mode: Regime misclassification at regime boundaries (ADX=24 vs 26, ATR percentile=39 vs 41). Frequent flip-flopping between quadrants causes whipsaw entries and exits. Requires a 3-bar stabilisation filter but that adds lag.
ideas.diversification_value: No existing regime filter in the archive proposes multiple sub-strategies selected by regime quadrant. Most detect regime then apply one strategy. This is an adaptive meta-strategy. Distinct from Hurst_Exponent_Regime_Detector (fractal), Gamma_Flip (options), Macro_Regime_Shifter (macro data), and Volatility_Cluster_Regime_Map (vol-only clustering).

ideas.name: Multi_TF_Vol_Convexity_Sizer
ideas.description: Position sizing overlay that detects volatility convexity divergence across timeframes — when short-term vol is compressing while long-term vol is expanding, the market is in a pre-breakout coil and standard sizing overexposes. Sizes down logarithmically when convexity inverts.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Calculate ATR(14) on M15, H1, H4 separately. 2. Compute the ratio of each to its 50-period median. 3. Define convexity = (H4_ratio / M15_ratio). 4. If convexity > 1.8 (long-term vol expanding faster than short-term vol is compressing — coil scenario), reduce base position by 60%. 5. If convexity < 0.6 (short-term vol far above long-term — panic spike scenario), reduce by 40% and tighten stop. 6. Normal convexity (0.8-1.2): use standard Kelly fraction.
ideas.exit_logic: Dynamic: position size is computed pre-trade as a fraction of the base Kelly amount. Trail stop using H1 ATR/2 when in profit > 1x H1 ATR. No hard TP — exit on convexity normalization or reversal signal from underlying strategy.
ideas.failure_mode: Fails in sustained trending markets where vol convexity stays extreme for days — would keep sizing down during the best part of a trend. Also relies on accurate ATR median baseline; a regime shift (e.g., COVID vol) makes the median stale instantly.
ideas.diversification_value: All existing risk_overlay entries manage static risk (fixed fraction, Kelly, VaR stop). This is the only one that reads vol STRUCTURE (short vs long timeframe divergence) rather than vol LEVEL. Adds orthogonal protection against pre-breakout whipsaw and post-spike stop-outs.

ideas.name: USD_Liquidity_Tide_Index
ideas.description: Liquidity-regime overlay using the US Dollar funding cycle as the primary driver of gold trend bias. Tracks reverse repo facility (RRP) drawdown, SOFR-IORB spread, and the DXY/BTC correlation regime to classify the market into Liquidity Flood, Neutral Drain, and Liquidity Crisis phases. Each phase flips the directional bias for XAUUSD entries.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Compute RRP Flow: (RRP_7d_ago - RRP_today) / RRP_7d_ago — positive means liquidity draining from system. 2. Compute SOFR Stress: SOFR - IORB spread, smoothed 3-day. 3. Compute DXY/BTC 20-day rolling correlation. 4. Classify regime: FLOOD (RRP flowing out > 20%, SOFR < 5bps, DXY/BTC corr < -0.5) → gold bullish, bias long. DRAIN (RRP stable, SOFR 5-15bps, DXY/BTC corr -0.5 to 0) → neutral, rely on primary strat. CRISIS (RRP drained < 10B remaining, SOFR > 20bps, DXY/BTC corr > 0) → dollar liquidity crisis, gold can crash WITH dollar — no entries allowed. 5. Only take XAUUSD trades aligned with FLOOD/DRAIN bias.
ideas.exit_logic: Exit when regime classification changes. If FLOOD → DRAIN, close 50% and trail rest. If any → CRISIS, close all immediately. No price-based TP — regime-based exits only.
ideas.failure_mode: Lagging indicator problem: RRP and SOFR data print with 1-2 day delay. Regime transition can happen intraday (a surprise Fed announcement flips everything). Also depends on continued RRP relevance — if the Fed changes facility terms, the indicator breaks.
ideas.diversification_value: All existing cross_asset ideas (DXY corr, gold/silver ratio, real yield) use price or yield data. This is the only one incorporating actual liquidity plumbing (RRP, SOFR) — the FUNDING side of the equation, not the pricing side. Orthogonal signal source.

ideas.name: News_Absorption_Continuation
ideas.description: Captures the directional continuation after high-impact news events (NFP, FOMC, CPI, PPI, Non-Farm Payrolls) by detecting the absorption pattern. After the initial 1-minute spike/kick, the market retraces into a consolidation zone. The side that successfully absorbs the retracement and breaks the initial spike high/low is the true direction.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Detect high-impact news event from economic calendar (filter: impact=high). 2. Let the 1-minute candle following the news print. Record its HIGH and LOW as spike bounds. 3. Wait for 3 full M15 candles after the news candle. 4. Plot a 20-EMA on M15. 5. If price breaks above spike high AND 20-EMA is sloping up → enter long. If breaks below spike low AND 20-EMA sloping down → enter short. 6. If after 5 M15 candles neither bound is broken, cancel — market is directionless after news. 7. Minimum ATR(14) on M15 > 15 pips to avoid low-vol events.
ideas.exit_logic: Hard SL at the opposite side of the initial spike bounds (e.g., long SL at spike low). TP1 at 1.5x initial spike range (close 50%). Remainder trails with 20-EMA on M15. Hard time stop: exit all at market close or 4 hours after entry, whichever comes first.
ideas.failure_mode: Fakeouts: price breaks spike high, triggers long, then reverses and pierces the other side. Most damaging during FOMC where multiple reversals happen within minutes. Also suffers from low sample rate — high-impact news is only ~8-12 events per month, making backtest statistical significance poor.
ideas.diversification_value: All existing other ideas (orderflow, session scalps, COT, pivot points) trade on structure/flow. This is the only event-driven idea tied to the macroeconomic calendar. It also explicitly waits for the retracement to absorb rather than chasing the initial spike — completely different risk profile from the existing scalpers.

ideas.name: Momentum_Entropy_Rotational_Sizer
ideas.description: Meta-momentum strategy that dynamically allocates capital across multiple momentum signals (ROC, ADX, MACD histogram slope) based on cross-signal entropy. When all momentum signals align (low entropy), concentrate capital on the highest-conviction pair. When signals diverge (high entropy), distribute evenly to avoid false-breakout whipsaws. This is a capital-allocation overlay, not a single entry rule -- it wraps existing momentum ideas into a rotational portfolio.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Compute 3 momentum signals per instrument: (a) 12-period ROC, (b) ADX trend strength, (c) MACD histogram slope over 5 bars. 2. Rank each signal across the watchlist (percentile rank 0-100). 3. Compute entropy H = -sum(p_i * log(p_i)) over the distribution of ranks -- low H means signals all point to the same instrument, high H means disagreement. 4. If H < threshold (coherent regime): allocate 60-80% of risk budget to the top-ranked instrument, split remainder equally. 5. If H >= threshold (divergent regime): allocate risk equally across all instruments (equal-weight model). 6. Rebalance every 4 hours on H1 or every H4 candle.
ideas.exit_logic: Stop Loss: 1.5x ATR(14) per position. Take Profit: 2x ATR(14) or when the momentum rank of the position drops below the 40th percentile (whichever comes first). Positions are also closed at rebalance if the instrument falls out of the top 3 by composite rank. Trailing stop activates at 1x ATR profit.
ideas.failure_mode: Killed by a regime of sustained low-volatility chop where all momentum signals are weak but erroneously show coherence -- capital concentrates on a pair with no real directional edge. Fails during black-swan gaps where rank-based allocation cannot react fast enough.
ideas.diversification_value: Unique in the archive as a multi-signal rotational meta-strategy rather than a single entry rule. No existing momentum idea dynamically shifts capital between instruments based on signal entropy. Complements Momentum_Confluence_Gold and MultiDecile_Momentum_Ensemble by adding a cross-instrument allocation layer.

ideas.name: Intraday_Volume_Profile_Mean_Reverter
ideas.description: Exploits the statistical tendency of price to revert to the high-volume node (HVN) of the current session volume profile. Unlike VWAP-based reversion (which tracks a single price line), this uses the full 3D volume distribution to identify the value area (70th percentile of volume). When price spikes more than 1.2x ATR above/below the value area boundary with declining delta, fade the move anticipating a return to the high-volume node.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Build a rolling 24-hour volume profile (VP) with 20-pip price bins. 2. Identify the value area: the price range containing 70% of total volume (search up/down from the peak volume node). 3. Mark the value area high (VAH) and value area low (VAL). 4. When price closes a 15m candle >= 1.2x ATR(14) above VAH with total delta (buy-sell volume) declining over the last 3 candles, enter short. 5. When price closes >= 1.2x ATR(14) below VAL with declining delta, enter long. 6. Additional filter: only trade when current volume is above the 20-period average volume (ensures meaningful VP formation).
ideas.exit_logic: Stop Loss: 0.8x ATR(14) beyond the entry extreme (so SL sits at 2.0x ATR from VAH/VAL). Take Profit: reversion to the high-volume node (HVN) -- the single price level with maximum volume. If the move is strong (delta re-accelerates), let it run to the opposite value area boundary (VAL on a short, VAH on a long) with a trailing stop of 0.5x ATR.
ideas.failure_mode: Fails in strong trend sessions where price never reverts to value area (e.g., NFP breakout or central bank surprise). The declining-delta filter helps but cannot prevent all trend-day losses. Also struggles in very low-volume sessions where the VP is unreliable.
ideas.diversification_value: Distinct from VWAP_Entropy_Mean_Drift and VWAP_Vol_Channel_Mean_Drift -- those use VWAP as a single line, while this uses the full volume profile distribution (VAH/VAL/HVN). Also different from Volume_Weighted_Mean_Reverter which uses cumulative volume at fixed levels. No existing idea uses VP value area boundaries as the mean-reversion trigger.

ideas.name: Central_Bank_Jawbone_Volatility_Capture
ideas.description: Captures the two-phase volatility pattern around central bank communication events (Fed speeches, FOMC minutes, ECB pressers, BoE rate decisions). Phase 1: position into the expected directional bias based on pre-event sentiment analysis from recent central bank language (hawkish/dovish drift). Phase 2: after the event, fade the knee-jerk spike if it exceeds 2.0 standard deviations of the typical event-range (measured over the last 20 comparable events), betting on news absorption and mean reversion within 30-60 minutes.
ideas.entry_logic: Phase 1 (Pre-Event Drift): 1. 30 minutes before scheduled event, parse recent central bank language sentiment (last 3 speeches/minutes). Score -3 (dovish) to +3 (hawkish). 2. If score >= +2, enter long at 0.3x standard risk. If score <= -2, enter short at 0.3x standard risk. 3. If score between -1 and +1, skip Phase 1. Phase 2 (Post-Event Fade): 4. Wait 5 minutes after release for initial spike to form. 5. Calculate event range = high - low of first 5-minute candle. 6. If event range > 2.0x average event range (computed over last 20 same-type events), fade the move: if price spiked above pre-event close, enter short at 0.5x risk; if price dropped below pre-event close, enter long at 0.5x risk. 7. If event range <= 2.0x average, do not fade.
ideas.exit_logic: Phase 1 exit: stop at 0.5x ATR(14) or exit 5 minutes before the event (whichever comes first). Take profit if price reaches 0.8x ATR in the intended direction. Phase 2 exit: stop at 1.0x ATR(14) from entry. Take profit at 1.5x ATR or 45 minutes after event (whichever comes first). Hard time-stop at 60 minutes post-event.
ideas.failure_mode: Killed by surprise policy shifts where the pre-event sentiment reading is wrong (e.g., Fed unexpectedly dovish when recent language was hawkish) -- both phases lose simultaneously. Also fails in low-volatility event regimes where the 2-sigma threshold is never breached and Phase 2 produces no trades.
ideas.diversification_value: No existing idea systematically trades both the pre-event drift AND the post-event volatility fade as a unified two-phase strategy. News_Absorption_Continuation trades post-news continuation (opposite direction), and Event_Volatility_Straddle_Reversal is a straddle-based approach. This is the first event-driven strategy combining directional pre-positioning with a volatility-mean-reversion fade.

ideas.name: MultiTimeframe_Liquidity_Stacked_Breakout
ideas.description: Identifies liquidity clusters stacked across H4, H1, and M15 order blocks at converging price levels. When price breaks through all stacked levels with a cascade of increasing volume (volume expansion >1.5x the 20-period average on each successive level break), it confirms genuine institutional absorption rather than retail liquidity grabs. The strategy measures the depth of liquidity at each level using volume profile and enters only when at least two consecutive timeframe levels break with volume confirmation.
ideas.market_behaviour: Gold exhibits multi-tiered liquidity structures where institutions place clusters of orders at key levels across timeframes. During accumulation, price repeatedly touches and rejects a level with decreasing volume (absorption). When the breakout finally occurs, volume cascades - each broken level releases the next tranche of stop-losses and adds momentum. Retail traders get caught guessing whether the first level break is real, while institutions use multi-level stacking to trap both sides. The Asian-to-London transition is the highest-probability window for this behavior.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Identify order blocks on H4, H1, M15 using standard ICT displacement + FVG methodology. 2. Check if any 2+ timeframes have order blocks overlapping within 0.3 ATR of each other (stacked liquidity zone). 3. Mark the outer boundary of the stacked zone as the trigger line. 4. Wait for price to break the trigger line with the first candle closing beyond it. 5. Confirm volume: the breakout candle range must be >= 1.5x the 20-period average candle range AND the tick volume (or delta) must show net directional dominance (>60% of volume in breakout direction). 6. Enter on the next candle open after confirmation. 7. If only one timeframe level breaks without volume confirmation, skip - treat as a false break.
ideas.exit_logic: SL = 1.5x ATR(14) on H1 measured from entry. TP1 = 2x ATR on H1 (50% position), TP2 = 4x ATR on H1 (remaining 50%). Trail TP2 at 1x ATR after TP1 is hit. Hard time-stop: exit if no new 0.5 ATR extension within 24 hours. If volume drops below average on any continuation candle after entry, tighten to a breakeven stop.
ideas.failure_mode: Fails in news-driven spike-and-retrace markets where volume spikes are from retail panic rather than institutional accumulation. Also fails during algorithmic chop where no clean multi-level structure exists - the strategy simply stays flat, which means long periods of inactivity. The multi-TF stacking requirement is a high bar and may miss genuine breakouts that only have one clean level.
ideas.diversification_value: Unlike single-level breakout strategies or retest-based breakouts, this requires explicit multi-timeframe liquidity stacking with volume cascade confirmation - a fundamentally different trigger condition. It operates in an entirely different signal space than momentum or mean-reversion bots and generates far fewer but higher-conviction signals. Complements existing Volume_Profile_Acceptance_Breakout by adding a stacked liquidity dimension.

ideas.name: Gold_USD_Cross_Rate_Carry_Trade_Proxy
ideas.description: Decomposes XAUUSD movements into two components: broad USD directional bias and gold-specific factors. By comparing gold price action against a USD index proxy constructed from the weighted average of EURUSD, GBPUSD, and USDJPY movements, the strategy isolates gold-specific strength/weakness. When gold and the USD proxy move in the same direction (gold rising while USD proxy also rising = gold outperforming USD weakness with additional gold-specific demand), conviction is high. When they diverge (gold rising while USD proxy falling = the move is just USD weakness), position sizing is halved and stops are tighter. This identifies pure alpha in gold rather than just beta from broad dollar moves.
ideas.market_behaviour: Gold's price is composed of roughly 60% USD directional component, 20% real-yield/inflation component, 10% geopolitical risk premium, and 10% residual (COMEX positioning, EM central bank accumulation, etc.). Most traders fail to distinguish between these drivers, taking gold trades that are really just USD trades. By decomposing the move, the strategy can size up when gold has genuine idiosyncratic demand (e.g., central bank buying, geopolitical panic) versus when it is just riding the dollar wave. The highest-RR setups occur when gold is rallying AGAINST a strengthening USD or falling against a weakening USD - these divergence signals precede regime changes in the gold-USD relationship.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Construct a synthetic USD index: USD_proxy = (0.576 * EURUSD + 0.136 * GBPUSD + 0.136 * USDJPY) using D1 returns, re-weighted to replicate DXY correlation. 2. Compute 20-period rolling correlation between XAUUSD D1 returns and USD_proxy returns. 3. ALSO compute 20-period rolling beta: gold_return = alpha + beta * USD_proxy_return + epsilon. 4. If correlation < -0.7 (standard inverse relationship) and beta magnitude > 1.2 (gold amplifies USD moves): standard sizing at 1x, SL = 1.5 ATR. 5. If correlation < -0.7 but beta < 1.0 (gold is muted vs USD moves): the gold-specific component is acting as a drag - HALVE position size. 6. If correlation is WEAK (> -0.5 or positive, meaning gold is moving independently): FULL size allowed because gold has genuine idiosyncratic demand - SL = tighter at 1.0 ATR. 7. Entry direction determined by which way gold breaks its H4 20-EMA after the correlation/beta analysis is complete.
ideas.exit_logic: Standard regime (step 4): TP = 2.5 ATR, SL = 1.5 ATR on H4. Muted regime (step 5): TP = 1.5 ATR, SL = 1.0 ATR (reduced tolerance). Independent regime (step 6): TP = 3.5 ATR, SL = 1.0 ATR (tight stop, wide target - capture the idiosyncratic move). All regimes: re-evaluate correlation/beta every 5 bars and exit if the regime classification changes (e.g., independent moves back to standard inverse - the idiosyncratic edge is gone).
ideas.failure_mode: In regime of perfectly predictable inverse correlation (beta ~-1, correlation ~-0.9), this strategy adds no edge over a simple DXY trend-following gold strategy - the decomposition has no divergence to exploit. The independent-move regime also can produce rare false signals (gold rallies on COMEX option expiration flows that reverse the next day). Requires reliable data for all 3 USD crosses which multiplies data feed failure risk.
ideas.diversification_value: Unlike DXY_Valence_Correlation which uses DXY level itself as a trigger, this strategy decomposes the gold-USD relationship into components (USD beta vs gold-specific alpha) and sizes based on which component is driving price. This is a higher-dimensional approach to gold trading that the existing cross_asset family lacks - it does not just use a correlation filter, it extracts and isolates the alpha component of gold moves.

ideas.name: Diwali_Chinese_New_Year_Physical_Demand_Frontrun
ideas.description: Front-runs the two largest global physical gold buying events: Diwali (Oct-Nov, India accounts for ~25% of global demand) and Chinese New Year (Jan-Feb, China accounts for ~30%). Three weeks before each event, historically gold enters a seasonal accumulation phase driven by wholesale/jewelry sector restocking. After the event, there is a predictable sell-off as physical premiums normalize and speculative longs unwind. The entry window is defined by calendar date with a confirmation filter requiring the 14-period RSI to be below 60 (not already overbought/pre-priced in). Takes profit in two tranches: half before the event, half after the post-event decline materializes.
ideas.market_behaviour: Physical gold demand follows a pronounced seasonal pattern driven by cultural festivals and wedding seasons. India's Diwali (festival of lights) is the single largest gold-buying period globally - households buy gold as auspicious investment and gifts. Chinese New Year drives similar buying for gifting and wealth storage. Wholesalers and jewelers typically begin stockpiling 2-3 weeks before each event, creating sustained upward pressure on spot gold. After the event, demand collapses and speculative longs (who front-ran the event) unwind, creating a 1-2 week retracement. This pattern has been consistent for 20+ years but is often overlooked by algorithmic traders who focus on technical or macro signals.
ideas.entry_logic: 1. Calculate Diwali date (variable Oct/Nov based on Hindu lunisolar calendar) and Chinese New Year date (variable Jan/Feb based on Chinese lunisolar calendar). Hard-code the 3-week pre-event windows. 2. 21 calendar days before event (T-21): open entry monitoring. 3. Confirm RSI(14) on D1 is below 60 (not overbought - rally has not been front-run already). 4.
